reasoning: The ما...ش circumfix wraps the verb (e.g. ما بعرفش maa ba3rafsh). Dots mark the verb slot. Genuine Palestinian verb negation alongside plain ما.
English 'block' taken as an Arabic verb, balak = he blocked (online). Recent loan slang used in Ramallah; past-tense he-form.
MSA-origin but the ordinary word Palestinians use for pollution. Shadda on و, ث kept as th here (learned noun).
Urban Palestinian merges ث to t, so ثانية is said taanye (cf. ثالث > تالت). Means a second of time, feminine.
Everyday Palestinian 'when', eemta; alif maqsura is final a. Dialectal as the English notes.

romanization: illi biyijri wara id-dinya maa biyil7a'ha
vowelled_arabic: اللي بِيِجْري وَرا الدِّنْيا ما بِيِلْحَقْها
reasoning: ق in يلحق is a glottal stop (biyil7a'ha). الدنيا assimilates to sun د. Common proverb; the English captures it.
MSA mawsim is said moosam in Palestinian, with a long o. Used for the agricultural/harvest season.
In learned words ذ surfaces as z in Palestinian (cf. لذيذ laziiz), so جذاب is jazzaab. Somewhat formal but used for attractive/charming.
بـ present tense bti3raf, ween for 'where'. The الـ... slot takes the noun. Natural Palestinian question frame to a male.
ص > S, ح > 7; il- assimilates to sun ص but stays before moon غ. Proper place name for Western Sahara.

meaning_fix: carbonated / fizzy (adjective, as in مشروب غازي); soda itself is gaazooz
reasoning: غازي is the adjective 'carbonated', not the noun 'soda' (that is gaazooz or mashruub ghaazi). Used in Ramallah but as a modifier.
مرة 'woman' in construct is marat; 3amm is paternal uncle, so marat 3amm = the wife of one's paternal uncle.
rub3 'quarter', keelo with long ee/oo. Everyday Palestinian for a quarter kilo.
ص > S. i3tiSaam is specifically a sit-in/standing protest, narrower than a generic 'protest' (muDaahara). Used in Palestinian news and speech.
ح > 7; 3ala 7saabi literally 'on my account' = my treat. Standard Palestinian.
English 'follow' borrowed for social-media follows. Loanword widely used by younger Ramallah speakers.
Construct form of nine used before a counted noun (tis3 + noun), e.g. tis3 iyyaam. Standard Palestinian.
From قلم with ق as a glottal stop and shadda on ل: m'allam = striped. Everyday Palestinian adjective.
ط > T. basiiT is simple/easygoing in everyday Palestinian.
3amme (taa marbuta as e) is the paternal aunt, so ibn 3amme is her son. Standard Palestinian kin term.
حرق with ق as glottal stop (7ara'); ض > D in akhDar. Idiom 'burned the green and the dry' = destroyed everything; used in Palestinian.
ط > T, ق glottal, shadda on ل: mTalla' = divorced (m.). Standard Palestinian.
ق is a glottal stop; the color is commonly said burtu'aani (final n) in Palestinian, though burtu'aali is also heard.
ح > 7. naja7 = he succeeded / passed. Everyday Palestinian past verb.
ص > S and il- assimilates to sun ص: si3r iS-Sarf = exchange rate. Used in Palestinian.
